routes.description: Establish that agents sometimes possess genuinely available alternatives under their control, that causal influence does not entail complete determination, and that this freedom supplies the agency presupposed by rational deliberation and responsibility.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if it supports alternative possibilities and agent control against the causal-completeness challenge, then shows why those capacities are required for reason-guided choice, moral desert, and justified responsibility practices.

motionBridge.description: Connect genuinely available, agent-controlled alternatives to the conditions under which responsibility and desert can be justified.

centralBridges.description: Establish that determinism's fixed-past consequence conflicts with the genuine ability to do otherwise.
Show that evidence of biological and environmental influence does not establish that every ordinary choice is completely determined.
Explain how agents can choose for reasons without those reasons deterministically necessitating a single outcome.
Show why responsibility and deserved treatment cannot be fully replaced by forward-looking causal management.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Defend a qualified presumption favoring experienced agency when decisive contrary evidence is absent.
Explain why deliberation, advice, and epistemic norms materially support control over action and belief.

routes.description: Establish that behavior arises from an uninterrupted interaction of biological and environmental causes, that intuition and indeterminacy do not supply independent agency, and that responsibility practices should follow causal and consequential considerations rather than desert.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if it supports a causally complete account of behavior, answers the principal proposed grounds for genuine alternatives, and explains how change, social regulation, and humane treatment remain possible without free will or retributive responsibility.

motionBridge.description: Connect the causal determination of action to rejection of freely deserved blame, reward, and punishment.

centralBridges.description: Establish a continuous, interacting causal account spanning immediate neural activity, development, environment, culture, ancestry, and evolution.
Show that no behaviorally effective contribution has been identified as independent of biological and environmental causes.
Explain why felt choice and ordinary responsibility judgments are insufficient evidence when mechanistic inquiry repeatedly revises intuition.
Account for behavioral change and justified social protection through causal intervention and consequences without invoking retributive desert.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Show that randomness or quantum indeterminacy does not by itself produce person-level control over which action occurs.
Relate expanding causal explanation to the reconsideration of blame and the adoption of less punitive responses.

sections.title: Causal completeness and the space for agency
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether the interacting biological and environmental history of behavior exhausts its explanation or leaves a distinct role for agent control.

sections.title: Alternative possibilities, determinism, and control
sections.rationale: This issue addresses the motion's core metaphysical question: whether a fixed causal past permits multiple genuinely available actions and control over which occurs.

sections.title: Intuition, scientific evidence, and the burden of proof
sections.rationale: This issue determines what evidential weight belongs to experienced agency, ordinary judgments, mechanistic findings, historical error, and the absence of complete prediction.

sections.title: Reasons, deliberation, and rational agency
sections.rationale: This issue examines whether choosing and believing for reasons require alternative possibilities or can be explained as causally determined responsiveness and change.

sections.title: Desert, punishment, and responsibility practices
sections.rationale: This issue connects the dispute about freedom to responsibility by testing retributive desert against deterrence, incapacitation, systemic consequences, and humane causal treatment.
